title: Neuroprotection in Perinatal Asphyxia through Environmental Enrichment and Palmitoylethanolamide: Correlation Between Morphological, Biochemical and Behavioral Markers
content: Perinatal asphyxia (PA) is an obstetric complication that disrupts oxygen supply at birth, leading to neuronal damage and increased risk of cognitive and neuropsychiatric disorders. Environmental enrichment (EE) has shown partial neuroprotective effects in PA cases, by improving synaptic function, reducing cell death, and enhancing cognitive recovery [1]. Similarly, palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) has demonstrated neuroprotective properties in PA models, mitigating hippocampal and striatal damage [2]. This study aims to assess whether combining EE and PEA enhances their therapeutic effects, offering a more effective intervention for PA-related impairments.
